insights.title: Your biological age was calculated: 54.5
insights.found: PhenoAge 54.5 years, from nine blood results on 20 Oct 2026. Your calendar age is 58.
insights.why: All nine inputs were measured, so the method could run.
insights.means: A lower biological than calendar age is a good sign, but this is research use only: the method was built on US adults, its coefficients are not yet re-verified, and it is not validated for clinical decisions. In studies, a higher PhenoAge than calendar age is linked to later kidney disease and higher mortality.
insights.do: Nothing to act on. Repeat it with your next blood tests to see the trend.
insights.expected: Your twin tracks it over time.
insights.helps: One number that summarises nine results.

insights.title: Screening for a hormonal cause of high blood pressure is recommended
insights.found: The 2025 Endocrine Society guideline suggests that everyone with high blood pressure be screened for primary aldosteronism with aldosterone, renin and their ratio.
insights.why: You have had high blood pressure since 2019, and your record has no aldosterone or renin test.
insights.means: Primary aldosteronism affects at least 1 in 10 people with high blood pressure and carries more heart risk than ordinary high blood pressure. Finding it changes treatment.
insights.do: Ask your doctor whether an aldosterone and renin test suits you.
insights.expected: Either a cause is found, or ordinary high blood pressure is confirmed.

insights.title: Home readings would show how well your blood pressure is controlled
insights.found: Your office blood pressure was 138/84 on amlodipine.
insights.why: Guidelines advise home monitoring for everyone on treatment; no home readings were supplied.
insights.means: Out-of-office readings predict heart and kidney outcomes better than office readings, and office readings misclassify control in most people.
insights.do: Use a validated upper-arm monitor with the right cuff size and record a week of readings.
insights.expected: Your doctor sees your real control.

insights.title: Your fasting glucose is in the prediabetes band
insights.found: Fasting glucose 5.8 mmol/L on 20 Oct 2026, with a BMI of 28.4.
insights.why: It is in the impaired-fasting-glucose band (5.6-6.9), and you are in the age and weight group screening guidelines cover.
insights.means: This is a risk state, not diabetes; about a third of people return to normal. Fasting glucose alone gives less risk information than HbA1c or a glucose tolerance test.
insights.do: Add HbA1c to your next panel; recheck fasting glucose in 6 to 12 months.
insights.expected: HbA1c gives your doctor a fuller picture.

insights.title: Your LDL cholesterol has not been measured on atorvastatin
insights.found: Total cholesterol 214 mg/dL and HDL 42 on 20 Oct 2026. You take atorvastatin. LDL, ApoB and Lp(a) are not in your record.
insights.why: Guidelines judge a statin by the percentage fall in LDL, checked 4-12 weeks after starting or changing the dose, then every 3-12 months.
insights.means: Without LDL your doctor cannot tell how well atorvastatin is working. ApoB predicts heart risk more accurately than LDL in most studies, and raised Lp(a) is common in South Asians.
insights.do: Add a full lipid panel with ApoB and Lp(a) to your next tests.
insights.expected: Your doctor sees whether atorvastatin is doing its job.

insights.title: Your 10-year heart and stroke risk is 7.3%
insights.found: The PREVENT equations give 7.3% for any cardiovascular disease in 10 years (5.1% for heart attack or stroke, 2.8% for heart failure) and 32.8% over 30 years.
insights.why: Every input the base model needs was in your record.
insights.means: These equations are not validated in Indian populations, and South Asian ancestry is a guideline-named risk enhancer, so your real risk may be higher than the number.
insights.do: Use it as a starting point in your next heart-risk discussion.

insights.title: A liver check is suggested for people with your risk factors
insights.found: The 2024 European guideline recommends checking for fatty liver with scarring in people with cardiometabolic risk factors.
insights.why: You meet several listed risk factors: BMI 28.4 (above 23 for Asian ethnicity), fasting glucose 5.8 and systolic 138 on treatment.
insights.means: The first step is a blood score (FIB-4), which needs AST, ALT and platelets, none of which are in your record.
insights.do: Ask for ALT, AST and a platelet count so FIB-4 can be calculated.
insights.expected: A simple blood score rules scarring in or out.

insights.title: Your kidney picture needs a urine test
insights.found: eGFR 74 (creatinine 88 umol/L) on 20 Oct 2026; urine albumin not measured.
insights.why: In Indian cohorts creatinine-based equations overestimate kidney function in the 60-89 band, and the 2026 heart-kidney-metabolic guideline adds urine albumin from stage 2.
insights.means: Your kidneys are probably fine, but a urine albumin test is needed to stage them, and cystatin C would make the eGFR more accurate.
insights.do: Add urine albumin, and cystatin C if your doctor agrees.

insights.title: Your inflammation marker is slightly raised
insights.why: It is at or above 2.0 mg/L, the JUPITER trial entry level.
insights.means: Informational only: one value cannot show lasting inflammation, and a recent infection makes it unreliable.
insights.do: Nothing to do now; it is repeated in a year or two.

insights.title: Your weight is above the Asian action point
insights.why: It is above 23.0, the WHO action point for Asian populations.
insights.means: This is informational and not a label of obesity. Your heart-health habits score gives BMI 70 of 100 and diet 25 of 100.
insights.do: Talk with your doctor about the food changes that suit you.
insights.expected: Weight, glucose and blood pressure tend to move together.

insights.title: Check whether your tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis booster is due
insights.found: Adults who never had Tdap should have one dose, then a Td booster every 10 years.
insights.why: Your vaccination history is not in your record.

eGFR 74 is in the mildly reduced band, and in Indian cohorts this equation tends to read high. A urine albumin test is needed to stage your kidneys; cystatin C would sharpen the eGFR.

glossary: PhenoAge
A published biological-age method (Levine 2018) that combines nine blood results with your age. Research use only.
PREVENT
The American Heart Association's 2023 risk equations for heart disease, stroke and heart failure.
eGFR
Estimated glomerular filtration rate: how well your kidneys filter, calculated from creatinine, age and sex.
Fasting glucose
Blood sugar after not eating for 8 hours or more.
HbA1c
Average blood sugar over about the last 2-3 months.
LDL / HDL
Two kinds of cholesterol in the blood. LDL is the main one linked to clogged arteries; HDL is often called 'good' cholesterol.
ApoB
A count of the particles that carry cholesterol into artery walls.
Lp(a)
Lipoprotein(a): a cholesterol particle whose level is mostly inherited; measured once in a lifetime.
hs-CRP
High-sensitivity C-reactive protein: a blood marker of inflammation.
BMI
Body mass index: weight divided by height squared.
Rule
One of our clinical checks. Each has a source, a threshold and an evidence grade; it fires only when your result clears it.
Primary aldosteronism
Too much aldosterone from the adrenal glands, a hormonal cause of high blood pressure.
FIB-4
A score from age, AST, ALT and platelets that estimates liver scarring.

F2.statement: Positive PhenoAgeAccel was associated with higher all-cause mortality in US adults, with a large hazard ratio. Biological-age measures may add risk stratification in multimorbid populations. This supports prognostic association in a general population, not validity or incremental value in essential hypertension.
F2.limitations: The abstract does not report adjustment for the individual risk factors, calibration, or discrimination beyond conventional risk scores. The hazard ratio is very large, which suggests the covariates and the clock inputs overlap. No hypertension subgroup is reported.
F2.population: US adults from NHANES; not hypertension-specific

F18.statement: In adults with moderate CKD (measured GFR 30-59), eGFR equations combining creatinine and cystatin C tracked change in measured GFR over 3 years better than creatinine-only CKD-EPI. All equations had low sensitivity (<54.1%) but high specificity (>90.4%) for detecting progression, so a single creatinine-based eGFR may underestimate decline. This supports considering cystatin C alongside creatinine when monitoring kidney function, but gives no testing interval.
F18.limitations: Population differs from this patient (eGFR 74, age 58, South Asian ancestry). No recommended retest interval. Estimated GFR underestimated the decline in measured GFR. Prognostic benefit of the more accurate equations is not shown.
F18.population: 1229 adults in England with CKD G3 (eGFR 30-59), median age about 67, 88% white. Not G2 and not South Asian.

F1.statement: In UK Biobank adults free of kidney disease, higher KDM-BA and PhenoAge acceleration were associated with incident CKD, with a stronger signal for PhenoAge and nonlinear relationships.
F1.limitations: Observational; creatinine and other kidney-related inputs may enter the clock, so some association may be mechanical. Ancestry mostly European, so applicability to South Asian individuals is uncertain. Quartile-contrast hazard ratios do not give absolute risk.
F1.population: 281,363 UK Biobank participants free of kidney disease at baseline; predominantly White.

F17.statement: The 2026 CKM guideline recommends staging by assessing metabolic risk factors, kidney function (eGFR) and CVD status. It recommends adding UACR assessment in CKM stage 2 and above and at least annual eGFR and UACR in those stages. This supports measuring albuminuria to determine this patient's risk stratum, but the excerpt shown contains no recommendation on SGLT2 or RAS inhibitor effects on eGFR slope in non-diabetic, normo-albuminuric adults.
F17.limitations: The excerpt omits the therapy sections. The recommendation concerns monitoring, not drug effect on slope. Evidence level is B-NR (non-randomized).
F17.population: Adults with or at risk for CKM syndrome, stage 2 and above for the annual eGFR plus UACR recommendation.

F11.statement: A systematic review of discordance studies (15 studies, 593,354 participants, including statin-treated and untreated patients) found apoB to be a more accurate marker of atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk than LDL-C in all 9 studies that compared them. ApoB was also more accurate than non-HDL-C in most studies. This is an association with risk prediction, not proof that apoB-guided therapy improves outcomes.
F11.limitations: Discordance analyses are observational. Heterogeneous methods. Only the abstract was available. Results for apoB versus non-HDL-C were mixed (one study favoured non-HDL-C, one found equivalence). Prediction is not treatment benefit.
F11.population: Mixed adult populations, with and without statins; statin-treated subgroup not separately quantified in the excerpt.
